SYNCERE raises $11 million pre-seed for its LUME home robot

The company plans to scale production and deliveries of its lamp-shaped home robot; capability and order figures are company claims.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗4 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Funding production and delivery

SYNCERE announced an $11 million pre-seed round led by a16z Speedrun. Founded by Aaron Tan and Angus Fung in Palo Alto, the company combines a floor lamp with a mobile household robot called LUME. The funding supports manufacturing, deliveries and further commercial applications.

A familiar household form

The supplier presents LUME as a lamp that can also fold laundry, tidy and make beds, with announced pricing from $2,699. It says deliveries have begun and preorders total millions of dollars. Preorders should not be treated as recognized revenue or confirmed delivered units.

Deployment still needs scrutiny

Personalized onboarding remains under development. The funding report does not provide independent evidence that every advertised task works across all homes. Human assistance, supported tasks and delivery terms still matter; the development is financing for scale, not proof of universal household autonomy.
